doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: The bus driver and finding hotels on the road
summary: A kindly bus driver found hotels for the band; rooms were shared two to a room.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You got to know what a bus was like I bet.

Well fortunately we had a nice bus driver, what was that man’s name now, oh boy. But he was a nice man. Because sometimes we’d come into town — he’d bring Hamp and his wife into town and we’d come into town and we would have nowhere to stay. And he’d take that bus and put us on the bus. He’d say “Come on guys, we’re going to find a decent hotel.” And he’d drive that bus and drive it around until we came up with a hotel. And he saw that everybody was signed in.
More like the road manager, then.
Yeah, yeah. He was something else. I’ll never forget him. As I say I’ll never forget him but I forgot the man’s name. Yeah. He was something else.
Did you guys have to pay for your own rooms?
Let’s see, yes. Sometimes, and sometimes not. It all depended.
So you were probably putting two and three guys in a room when you could.

Well at least two in a room, yeah. No we didn’t have three but two would be in a room mostly. He’d try to give us single rooms. Because a lot of the guys didn’t like doubling up. Me? I was one of them. I didn’t like that doubling up.
